The role of gender in society is complex, with intersections within race, class, and culture. With regard to western societies, my belief is that open dialogue on gender roles and related topics is essential to create a fair and just society.

Gender roles are not dictated by any single culture, but by the people and structures of society. In different cultures gender roles change over time as society evolves, and men and women adopt new roles. Whenever people are truly free to choose the roles they want to occupy, society benefits from greater innovation and creativity.

Current gender discourse sometimes ignores the fact that within identity, people can encompass a range of relationships, identities and orientations, and that not all identities are contingent on what others view as types of sexual or gender roles.

In sum, while differences of gender are important, I believe that the ways gender is understood and expressed can and should evolve for the better.
